answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, non-transferable deposit before it may submit jobs or vote on task results. The protocol weights influence by the deposit, not by the number of identities, and slashes it when independently checked work is fraudulent. An attacker can still create a spiral of fake accounts, but each account needs fresh capital and risks losing it; splitting one deposit among identities buys no extra weight. The inlet stays open to newcomers, while honest agents can grow a garden of reputation through verified work.
